candidates.title: I'm 40. If you’re in your 20s, read this.
candidates.summary: In your 20s, it’s tempting to think your life needs to be planned out. I quickly learned this was a lie. It appears as though everyone you look at on social media who is also in their 20s has life figured out. That’s bullsh*t. Nobody has their life all figured out. Not even at 40. Especially at 40.
candidates.full: In your 20s, it’s tempting to think your life needs to be planned out. I quickly learned this was a lie. It appears as though everyone you look at on social media who is also in their 20s has life figured out. That’s bullsh*t. Nobody has their life all figured out. Not even at 40. Especially at 40. You think you choose a path and walk down it. That’s not true anymore. Life has gone from a linear progression of events to a total non-linear adventure. Technology has enabled this reality. It creates uncertainty, but it’s also a huge opportunity. My 20s were full of alcohol, parties, bad decisions, and having no idea what career I would pursue. As soon as I thought I had it all figured out, my life collapsed around me. My mental health got so dark, I didn’t want to live anymore. But I escaped my 20s. They taught me a lot. I wish I’d known what I know now about being 20-something. Here are the powerful lessons that’ll help you. This is the most bizarre lesson I have for you. When I was 20-something, I wanted an easy life. I felt resentful that I grew up with constant money problems. I felt resentful that the school system rejected me and that I didn’t get to go to college. It left me bitter and twisted. I drank to distract myself. Now I see hard times differently. 20 years have passed. The friends who grew up with rich parents, inheritances, or who went to fancy private schools are mostly losers. They became entitled. Most of them got into drugs. They’ve never worked hard. Daddy always comes in to bail them out. My friends who, like me, had a hard life now have a much easier life at 40. We know the value of hard work. We don’t ask for handouts. We have to earn every opportunity. We’re much more humble. We don’t have a giant pole up our ass. And we have zero desire to impress people with luxury brands and sports cars. Things get even more bizarre. I now crave a hard life. I don’t want things to come easy. I love the pain and brutality of having things not go right. I learn more from failure than from any info product or $100K degree. Hormozi has an interesting perspective here: Everything is hard. Nothing works the first time. It all feels pointless. That’s when you realize you’re going to have to will it into existence with every ounce of your f*cking soul. And that’s when it starts to happen. Wanting it to be easy steals away your personal power. It makes you lazy and makes you want to chase passive income that doesn’t exist. In retrospect, the greatest opportunity I’ve ever been given is a hard life. It makes me appreciate simple things much more. And it makes me more resilient to face hard times, tragedies, and new opportunities where I feel like a fraud. The same applies to you. You can either use the hard times as a reason to become a victim, or you can use them as an opportunity. If you do come from a privileged upbringing, then it’s time to do more hard things and reject an easy life. Here’s what is weird: Even if you think you want someone’s life, you’re highly likely to only be viewing the highlight reel. Life is an iceberg. The people who seem to be winning are often the most miserable f*cks on the planet. Just spend time around insanely rich people or high society like I did. It made me want to vomit. A lot of rich people think they’re god’s gift to humankind and they treat their fellow humans like slaves. Before you model your life on someone else, spend time with them. Pay them for coaching. Join their mastermind. Have coffee with them. Just don’t sit there thinking everyone is winning. Their career could be great, but that means their marriage is probably trash. Their kids could be perfect, but that means their financial situation could be terrible because they didn’t spend enough time working. The business they built could be cool, but they have zero time for their two sons who never see them and pray to see their daddy. Nothing is as it seems. Most of the time you should just follow your own path. I love my two daughters. Feminists on the internet attack me all the time for being daddy-first. They try to make me feel guilty for having kids or for describing it as blissful. They assume I must never have changed a diaper, because if I did, I’d say that having kids sucks. Again, they didn’t read the first point of this essay. I love hard things. It’s a f*cking privilege to change both my daughters’ diapers and get covered in piss and poo. Why? Because many of my friends have tried to have kids and failed. They’ve gone through years of IVF, or worse, had their unborn baby die 8 months in. This is more common than people think. So yes, having kids is hard, but that’s why it’s an opportunity some people should consider. There’s zero obligation to have kids. Everyone’s situation is different. But to insist all fathers are lazy and have it easy is a lie. The modern father like me shares the load. Don’t rule out kids just because a bunch of raging feminists are mad at men for who knows what. Blindly dismissing an entire gender because you met a few bad men/women is low IQ. Same applies to race. 20-somethings should think carefully about kids. No one tells you this. The cool people in my 20s who drank every day and partied hard are still trying to do that at 40. The bullies in high school were cool and had the hottest girlfriends. Now some of those morons are still trying to bully me online — except they’re unemployed, single, hating life, and angry. I’m not. Stop trying to be cool as young as you possibly can. What’s cool at 40 is very different from what’s cool in high school. Cool at 40 means having freedom, moderate wealth, an I-don’t-give-a-f*ck attitude, not attending an adult daycare, not having other adults tell you what to do, and being yourself. Implement that way of life as young as possible. The happiest people at 40 are the ones who got what they wanted out of life. They’re the ones who made a plan, had goals, and went for them. I’m obsessed with former chef and TV presenter Anthony Bourdain. But there’s a lot I don’t like about him, such as his joking about taking his own life. He is perhaps the most traveled man to ever live. He had it all. Yet it wasn’t enough. He took his own life. Travel writer Cailey Rizzo idolized Bourdain. She mimicked his life. She spent time with him too. She traveled endlessly, too, and came to a harsh realization: I began to realize that going to different countries wasn’t a solution to a life. I had stopped being able to outrun my problems. Eventually, life on the road just becomes regular life. Whereas most people escape for adventure, when you’re a travel writer, you start craving an escape to stability. But people keep telling you that you have a dream job. With my head over the toilet, I came up with a plan to k!ll myself. It wasn’t about the fruit. It was about the fact that I was living out my dreams and I couldn’t feel anything. Life was meaningless and I saw only one way out. I was going to get a gun. I wasn’t going to leave a note. You’re better off facing reality. When I went to different countries I started to notice that they all looked the same. I realized I craved a place that felt like home more than changing countries all the time, looking for a new family or new friends. Once I found a home and made peace with my family, my desire to travel disappeared. I now travel much less. I love home. I love my neighbors. I love being around friends. This is what the good life secretly looks like. If you’re 20 then travel. But if you’re doing it to escape, at some point soon, your world is going to come crashing down once you realize it’s not the answer to your problems. (Cormac McCarthy) In my early 30s, I was at work one afternoon. A banker from Sydney stopped me in the hallway on the way to lunch. I was pissed. He made me late. He kept me talking for 15 minutes about stupid risk stuff that bored me to tears. When I walked outside, I saw chaos. A man drove his car up the sidewalk and killed loads of innocent people. The police shot out his tires right after he ran over a stroller with a newborn baby. The baby died. It’s one of Australia’s worst mass murders. Had I gone to lunch on time, wearing my headphones like I always do, I would have been standing right where the car hit people. I’d have died. My bad luck saved me from worse luck. Bad luck in your 20s is not all bad. It shields you from even worse luck. Perhaps you got caught doing something silly. If you learned the lesson, then that probably stopped you from doing something criminal. Bad luck is a blessing. If you think hard enough, you’ll realize what piece of media that was for you. For me, the piece of media that changed my life was a DJ set by the artist Axwell. I watched it and it led me to become a DJ. I spent years working in strip clubs and nightclubs chasing that dream. I drank heavily when I got rejected for better gigs. I really wanted that DJ dream. But in my 20s, I didn’t understand the basics of self-improvement. I was entitled. I thought short-term. I was lazy. I wanted a lucky break. I thought the music I produced as an artist signed to a record label was good (it was terrible). And I wasn’t willing to do any sales or marketing. The irony is my friend I studied sound engineering with achieved his DJ goal. Still to this day he is one of the most famous DJs globally. For years, he played in nightclubs and stadiums and resisted the urge to take drugs. He made it nearly 15 years completely clean. Eventually drugs got him. He’s now addicted to hard drugs. At 40, I now understand that being a DJ is just being an entertainer for people out of their minds on pills. And that if I did stay a DJ, I would eventually have to take drugs to advance my career and truly understand the audience of drug addicts. Getting everything you think you want in your 20s is often a nightmare. Not getting what you want is the savior. MIT professor Patrick Winston gave a famous lecture every 20-something should watch. He says: “Your success in life will be determined largely by your ability to speak, your ability to write, and the quality of your ideas, in that order.” This is even more true in a world of AI. Not all skills are equal. The more human skills now carry a much larger ROI than before. This is why I’m obsessed with writing. It’s how you join the dots between your ideas and refine them. Those ideas also act as a magnet for the right people. Writing & public speaking should be mandatory skills to pass high school and college. Writer Jay Alto said this: “You pity the moth confusing a lamp for the moon, yet here you are confusing a screen for the world.” The internet looks like real life. It’s not. Neither is AI. Since 2020 people mistake their phones for reality. What happens online isn’t everything. The physical world is different. If you spend too much time online, you lose your edge. It’s how people developed ChatGPT brain after 2022. I kid you not, there are 20-somethings everywhere who can’t think without having ChatGPT help them. They believe thinking is asking ChatGPT instead of asking themselves. They take the opinion of an AI as fact instead of their own experience. Then they wonder why they get sh*t results. AI is trained on normie content. On 101 tutorials. You’re getting the same answer as everyone else when you rely on it. Real wisdom comes from failure, rejection, experiments, and interacting with humans. Be pro-tech for sure, but don’t mistake it for real life. It’s easy in your 20s to think you’re crushing it. Youth inflates your ego and makes you forget your immaturity, lack of experience, and naivety. Philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche has an excellent way to check yourself before you wreck yourself. What is the history of every day in your case? Look at your habits that constitute it: are they the product of innumerable little cowardices and lazinesses, or of your courage and inventive reason?” If you talk to the average 40 year old, you’ll find (like I have) that their days are made up of innumerable little cowardices and lazinesses. And they’ll do anything they can not to admit it. All you have to do is look at their decisions. Most of them don’t make decisions. They see an opportunity, then delay making a decision and end up stuck with indecision. This is cowardice. I know because I practiced this habit for 10 years and it kept me trapped in a banking career like the prisoner of Azkaban. Do one tiny courageous act every day of your 20s to win back your life one day at a time. 20-somethings are made fun of all the time. Older people tell them to shut up and listen. That they need to fall in line and listen to a guru’s wisdom. I used to believe this too. Not anymore. Earlier in my career, I got to work with the founders of Stripe. They entered the competitive field of banking at a young age. They had no idea about risk, compliance, or banking. My employer ridiculed them for being naive. The Collison brothers, who founded Stripe, ended up becoming wildly successful. When I heard their story firsthand, I realized that being naive is a superpower. When you’re too dumb or inexperienced to know any better, you don’t see rules or limitations. “This can’t be done” doesn’t enter your mind. And old, outdated systems don’t apply because you’ve never heard of them. In my late 20s, something happened to me. I started figuring out social media at an aggressive level. I had no idea what I was doing. I didn’t understand the writing world, publications, or “prose.” I just published like a psycho. Not knowing how the writing world worked ended up being my advantage because I helped come up with a new way of doing things. Being too naive to know any better is how you create something new. It’s never too late to reinvent yourself. This dude, Gunnar Holm, says his dad’s uncle is a great example. Pursued gymnastics and ended up at the Olympics. Began playing golf at 36. Within 2 years he got a handicap of 2. Then quit golf and started making music. In a few short years, he went on to produce Björk’s first album. People who can reinvent themselves multiple times succeed wildly in life. Because reinvention requires an ability to change. And once you hit 40 like I have, you start to see that most people love the idea of change but aren’t willing to actually change. Sad. In a world where linear careers are dying because of AI, your ability as a 20-something to constantly reinvent yourself, learn new skills, and change careers is critical. Being unwilling to change is a death sentence. In your 20s, you’re taught to self-promote like crazy. But this advice has a dangerous dark side. You end up falling in love with yourself. You end up writing books, launching podcasts, and posting on social media to serve yourself. And when you do that nobody cares because you’re obsessed with you and your pretty little f*cking legacy. My friend Justin Welsh said this: “The people who really matter are too busy teaching someone else. They don’t even have time to care about their own reputation. They know something the rest of us miss: When you pour yourself into developing others, you become immortal in a way that no amount of self-promotion can ever match.” That’s what I now know at 40. Be helpful and you’ll never have to promote yourself again. Word of mouth and your results will do the heavy lifting. Your reputation will come from the people you’ve helped, not sleazy “marketing.” Most people in their 20s are controlled by money. They do things they don’t want to do because they need the money. But when you no longer need the money, you get to decide what things you will do. And you get to say no to a lot more things too. The fastest way I found to get richer was to lower my desire for bullsh*t luxury. When you don’t need a $500K sports car and a $5M McMansion to feel secure, you don’t need to make as much money. So you hit financial freedom faster. There are 4 levels to getting good with money: Get the right skills (skills = money) Make plenty of money Learn how to keep money Get good at investing money, so your money makes more money If you screw up any level of the money game, you struggle by default with money. And money will control you for as long as you’re alive. There’s no certainty when you’re 20-something. There’s also zero certainty at 40. Needing certainty is a virus. It stops people from living life and doing things. No one knows if an opportunity will work out. What is certain is that doing nothing will get you nowhere, and likely lead to regrets. The best paths in life come from embracing uncertainty. They come from knowing if you take action and are committed to figuring it out, then you will. If you only want to say yes if the outcome is certain or guaranteed, life is gonna be a struggle. What is certain is you will fail and get rejected a lot before you learn anything. What is certain is that winners lose a lot, which is why they win. Fear of losing leads to never winning. Your 20s are full of pain. Ironically, for me, the more painful a situation is the more nostalgia I have. When you’re in the arena it’s not something your mind can easily forget. The hard days of unloading containers at midnight in blistering hot weather with my brother and no fork lift felt like hell on earth. Now I crave those days. Same with when I worked in a call center. At the time, I was on minimum wage and a micromanager timed my piss breaks. It felt like prison. Now I wish I could go back. It’s where I learned all the skills I have now. And it’s where I met some incredible people. The painful parts of life are the best when you hit 40. No one wants to be lonely in their 20s. I found it useful. Loneliness taught me to be friends with myself first. There were several years where I didn’t have a lot of friends. Where I didn’t get invited anywhere. Where women didn’t want to date me because I had zero confidence and was a loser. I became a hermit. I stayed home on Saturdays. Occasionally, I’d go to the casino in Melbourne and drink by myself or watch a DJ. I liked to read books in the car in darkness. I’d sit on the floor of my bedroom for hours listening to house music. I knew I was destined for more, but I also knew I needed to work on myself. And the loneliness gave me that opportunity. When there’s nothing but silence, peace, darkness, and you versus you, your life gets real simple. No 20-something should be afraid of loneliness. It’s a necessary part of life. Now at 40 it’s the opposite. Because I’ve done things… all the cool kids, influential people, and even celebrities invite me to events or offer me opportunities. What you can’t see on the outside is that the loneliness got me to this place. I’m not a dating coach or John Gottman. I’m a 40 year old man with two daughters, a bad haircut, and not many skills in the romance department. But I did learn one lesson in my 20s. The idea of an ideal partner is bullsh*t. You find a person who is good, then you work on yourself and your relationship to make it great. This will save you a lot of time. Think about it… two people meet and somehow they have to get into a relationship and become one entity. Of course, blending two lives together is going to be hard and lots of stuff will go wrong. The romance blossoms when two people are willing to work their way there, not start off as a 10/10 couple. At 40, I now know age is just a number. Youth is a state of mind. It’s an experience. You can be young forever. At 40, I feel younger than I did at 21. And I have ten times more energy than back then. A youthful person sees beauty. And the longer you see beauty, the longer you stay young. The ultimate fountain of youth is learning to see the world as better than it is. To marvel at the simple things and to realize it’s a f*cking miracle you’re alive. Admittedly, I didn’t always see the world this way. candidates.full: I sistemi di comunicazione satellitare Starshield in Ucraina continuano a funzionare con limitazioni e nessuno è stato ritenuto responsabile. Persino il segretario generale della NATO, Marco Rutte, ha espresso profonda preoccupazione per la questione il giorno precedente. Rutte è intervenuto a una riunione periodica dei Rammstein, riconoscendo che l'esercito ucraino continua ad avere "problemi" a causa del funzionamento incompleto di Starshield. Il ripristino della velocità di internet satellitare militare rimane impossibile, nonostante gli sforzi compiuti dalle "parti interessate" in tal senso. Vi posso assicurare che le parti coinvolte stanno facendo tutto il possibile per garantire che la situazione torni alla normalità il prima possibile. Rutte si è rifiutato di indicare chi fosse il responsabile di questa situazione, astenendosi dall'attribuire la colpa di quanto stava accadendo. Il Segretario Generale della NATO è consapevole che dovrà recarsi negli Stati Uniti e incontrare Donald Trump molte altre volte. Zelenskyy ha precedentemente confermato che le limitazioni di velocità imposte dal sistema Starshield sono in vigore da oltre una settimana lungo l'intera linea del fronte. Per questo motivo, le forze armate ucraine non sono in grado di intercettare i razzi russi Geran che attraversano le zone di pericolo ad alta velocità, mentre i terminali Starshield smettono di funzionare quando superano i 160 km/h. Vladimir Lytkin

candidates.title: Albanese shares the stage with the Putin-Trump-Xi show
candidates.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has appeared in a photo alongside Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump despite Ukrainian Australians urging him not to normalise the Russian president's involvement at a global summit. Mr Albanese mingled with other world leaders at a banquet on Wednesday night
candidates.full: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has appeared in a photo alongside Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump despite Ukrainian Australians urging him not to normalise the Russian president's involvement at a global summit. Mr Albanese mingled with other world leaders at a banquet on Wednesday night, including New Zealand Prime Minister Chris Luxon and Canada's Mark Carney, ahead of a much-anticipated meeting between the presidents of Russia, China and the United States at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. While the Australian and Canadian prime ministers both condemned Mr Putin's invasion of Ukraine, they chose not to boycott the photo at the request of their Chinese hosts. Canadian and Australian foreign ministers refused to appear in a photo with Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov in October. It comes before Mr Putin, Mr Trump and Mr Xi hold an unprecedented meeting on Thursday, where nuclear proliferation is likely to be a key talking point. But critics have said the unprecedented meeting could result in a re-run of the 1945 Yalta conference, in which the US, Britain and the Soviet Union divided the ruins of Europe into competing spheres of influence. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has raised his concerns about the major powers deciding the fate of Ukraine against the wishes of the former Soviet member state. As he arrived in China on Wednesday, Mr Putin derided Western sanctions on Russia. Instead, he argued, they had made Russia stronger, while Europe was stuck in a "humiliating decline". But Mr Carney hit back at Mr Putin, claiming the former KGB agent was lying about the financial situation on the ground in Russia. Mr Albanese said there was still a role for middle powers, like Canada and Australia, to use their influence on the global stage. He reiterated Australia's support for Ukraine, and condemned Russia for its "illegal and immoral" invasion. As well as Mr Carney, Mr Albanese will meet with the leaders of Mexico, South Korea and New Zealand on Thursday. He will likely continue to spruik the benefits of Australia's plan for artificial intelligence safety standards, after Mr Carney called for global governance on AI. AI could bring new prosperity to the Asia-Pacific region as long as safety, security and social licence were assured, Mr Albanese said in a speech to the APEC CEO summit. Australian Associated Press

candidates.summary: The Morning Risk Report: Commerce Department Moves to Crack Down on Chip Exports Good morning. candidates.full: The Morning Risk Report: Commerce Department Moves to Crack Down on Chip Exports Good morning. The Commerce Department issued a long-awaited rule to crack down on shipments of chips from Nvidia and other U.S. companies to China, the latest sign of how the Jensen Huang saga is influencing the Trump administration’s policies. Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil will be added to a list of countries subject to export restrictions, and companies will need licenses from the Commerce Department to ship to those countries, a step intended to prevent Chinese customers from accessing data-center capacity in those countries remotely. U.S. tech companies could get exceptions. Avoiding a repeat: The goal is to crack down on companies like Megaspeed International, where Alice Huang, who was a top executive and suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, was having an affair with Jensen Huang, who stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive last week. Companies like Megaspeed have used billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips to build data centers throughout Southeast Asia and provide computing power to Chinese tech giants seeking to catch up in the artificial-intelligence race. Commerce pressure: The Commerce Department has been under pressure from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other officials who have accused it of moving too slowly to address export-control loopholes. In one sign of that strain, a Commerce release said the rule was “written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council.” Export-control analysts said it was an unusual step for other agencies to take control of the rule-making process from BIS, which is normally in charge of chip-export measures. Blame game: Bessent last week said that Treasury and other agencies had been pushing for action on Megaspeed and chip exports for months but Commerce stood in the way. The turmoil has increased pressure on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is receiving much of the blame inside the administration, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Immediate effects: The rule takes effect immediately, but companies will have 60 days to offer comments. Shares of many AI and data-center companies including Advanced Micro Devices and CoreWeave fell about 5% or more following the announcement. Nvidia was down about 4%. Its shares have slumped amid the CEO turmoil, helping drag down the broader sector. California filed a lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the company misled and endangered the public by knowingly developing AI models without necessary safeguards. The suit is the latest in a series of legal actions that reflect growing concerns about the dangers of rapidly advancing artificial-intelligence technology. California’s attorney general alleged in the suit that the July Hugging Face attack, in which rogue OpenAI agents breached their internal environment, was foreseeable given OpenAI’s decision to test models in a flawed way, and without proper oversight. The suit, which was filed in San Francisco Superior Court, alleges OpenAI knew the AI models were dangerous. The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Facebook-parent Meta nearly $900 million for violating users’ privacy, claiming that their photos were accessed without consent, Risk Journal’s Yusuf Khan reports. (free link) The authority fined Meta €805 million ($886 million) saying that photos and videos from Android users’ phones were accessed without their agreement. The Italian authority had been investigating the issue of privacy since July 2025. It found that a feature in Facebook called “’Get camera roll suggestions when you’re browsing Facebook” allowed for the company to access a user’s camera roll on a permanent basis. That access was given through a single permission. The authority said Facebook didn’t make it clear to users that their entire library of photos could be accessed. Nvidia is creating a board committee to oversee national-security and export controls, one of the company’s first moves after a geopolitical firestorm over former CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Nine Democratic senators including Adam Schiff (Calif.), Amy Klobuchar (Minn.) and Elissa Slotkin (Mich.) this morning sent a letter to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission asking it to freeze its efforts to assert its regulatory authority over prediction markets. Intel is being sued by shareholders who claim the U.S. chip maker failed to disclose the scale of a slump in personal-computer sales that contributed to shares plunging nearly 29% in a single day last month. Roche Holding received the green light from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to launch a new pill to treat advanced breast cancer, the first approval for what executives say could become the company’s top-selling product. Risk Journal reports: The European Union imposed sanctions on oil traders based in the United Arab Emirates as part of a fresh round of restrictive measures against Russia. The value of Tesla’s investment in a new facility in its German factory as the company seeks to boost production of its autonomous Cybercab. Examine data on the economics of AI — from Anthropic’s pricey models to low-cost Chinese competitors — and what pricing differences reveal about AI competition, the sustainability of premium pricing and financial decisions businesses face as they expand their use of AI. Register to join the webinar at 10 a.m. ET on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Chinese leader Xi Jinping is confronting a precarious moment in his global diplomatic offensive, as the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs relations with Washington ahead of an unprecedented trilateral gathering with President Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin. The resignation of Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang over an affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence is undermining Xi’s message that he has successfully stabilized ties with the U.S., and will overshadow China’s carefully choreographed optics this week to place China on equal footing with Washington and Moscow. The company bought FB securities, a small New York-based broker, in July and plans to launch equity trading within the next two months, people familiar with the matter said. As artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic prepares to go public, a wide-ranging group of investors including venture-capital firms, leading technology companies and sovereign-wealth funds are preparing for enormous windfalls. At least $154 billion in flows linked to criminal activity passed through cryptocurrency exchanges each year from 2021 to 2025, researchers at the University of Texas at Austin said. When President Trump boarded Air Force One on Monday for a long-haul flight to Asia, he brought with him a team of top advisers who have spent the past week feuding over China policy and slinging blame at one another for the political fallout from the Nvidia scandal. candidates.full: Google запустив безкоштовну гру українською, яка навчить школярів працювати зі ШІ Для вчителів проведуть презентацію Google переклав українською мовою інтерактивну освітню гру AI Quests, яка допомагає дітям віком 11–14 років зрозуміти, як працює штучний інтелект і де його застосовують у реальному житті. Грати можна безкоштовно, навички програмування чи попередній досвід роботи з ШІ не потрібні. Про це повідомило Міністерство освіти і науки України. Проєкт створили команди Google Research спільно зі Stanford Accelerator for Learning. Його реалізували за підтримки МОН, Міністерства цифрової трансформації та платформи Дія.Освіта. Гра пропонує не просто дізнатися про штучний інтелект, а спробувати самостійно навчити його розвʼязувати різні завдання. У вигаданому світі підлітки разом із персонажем професоркою Скай проходять квести, засновані на реальних наукових дослідженнях Google. Під час гри школярі збирають та аналізують інформацію, навчають моделі штучного інтелекту, перевіряють їхні прогнози й виправляють помилки. Так вони можуть побачити, чому для роботи ШІ важлива якість даних і як людські рішення впливають на результат. Не пропустіть найважливіше Додайте ZAXID.NET у вибрані в Google Наразі українською доступні два квести: - «Топкий ринок» присвячений прогнозуванню повеней. Учасники аналізують дані про кількість опадів і рівень води в річках, обирають параметри для навчання моделі та перевіряють, наскільки точно вона може передбачити стихійне лихо. Завдання демонструє, як ШІ може допомагати завчасно попереджати громади про небезпеку. - «Присмеркові дюни» знайомить із використанням штучного інтелекту в медицині. candidates.full: Названі найпроблемніші двигуни на популярних автомобілях Сучасні 4-циліндрові двигуни відомих брендів стали основною робочою силою світового автопрому, адже поєднують компактність, економічність та хорошу динаміку. Проте масове виробництво й ускладнення конструкції нерідко призводять до серйозних інженерних прорахунків. Експерти зібрали чотири історії невдалих моторів, які обернулися для компаній багатомільйонними штрафами та масовими відкликаннями. Про це пишуть Новини.LIVE з посиланням на Jalopnik. Корейський скандал Сімейство бензинових агрегатів Hyundai/Kia серії Theta II об'ємом 2 та 2,4 л стало хрестоматійним прикладом виробничого браку. У 2015 році корейці оголосили відкликання близько 470 000 Hyundai Sonata 2011–2012 років через металеву стружку, яка залишалася на колінчастому валу після механічної обробки на заводі в Алабамі. Це сміття швидко руйнувало шатунні вкладиші та призводило до заклинювання мотора. Скандал набув гігантських масштабів, коли на порталі CarComplaints Sonata 2016 року зібрав понад тисячу скарг з середнім пробігом до поломки лише 39 360 км. У підсумку концерн погодився виплатити 1 300 000 000 доларів компенсацій. Додатково регулятор NHTSA у 2020 році оштрафував Hyundai/Kia на 210 000 000 доларів за затягування відкличної кампанії для понад 1 600 000 машин. Вогняний Ford Турбований двигун Ford EcoBoost об'ємом 1,6 л запам'ятався власникам схильністю до займання під капотом. Лише протягом 2012 року виробник тричі відкликав кросовери Escape та седани Fusion через пошкоджені паливні магістралі та витік антифризу, який спалахував при потраплянні на гарячу вихлопну систему. У листопаді 2013 року довелося ремонтувати ще майже 140 000 кросоверів через тріщини в головці блока циліндрів від перегріву, а у 2017 році під нову сервісну кампанію через ризик пожежі потрапили вже 208 584 машини. Окрім загрози загоряння, цей агрегат часто страждає від потрапляння охолоджувальної рідини в циліндри. Власники на профільних форумах зазначають, що така несправність є лише питанням часу і майже завжди закінчується дорогим капітальним ремонтом. Змінний тиск Інноваційний двигун Nissan/Infiniti сімейства VC-Turbo зі змінним ступенем стиснення (3-циліндровий 1,5 л та 4-циліндровий 2 л) спочатку вважали технологічним проривом, але згодом він обернувся серією великих відкликань. У червні 2025 року компанія відкликала 443 899 автомобілів Nissan Rogue, Altima та моделей Infiniti через передчасне руйнування підшипників. У лютому 2026 року додалися ще дві кампанії для сотень тисяч кросоверів Rogue через деградацію оливи від перегріву, пробиття блока циліндрів з ризиком пожежі та поломку шестерні в електронній дросельній заслінці. Загалом під сервісні акції потрапили понад мільйон машин з моторами VC-Turbo. Пісок у гібриді Турбомотор 2 л у плагін-гібридних позашляховиках Jeep 4xe підвела не конструкція, а порушення технології на заводі постачальника. У листопаді 2025 року концерн Chrysler оголосив відкликання 112 859 гібридів, позаяк з виливків блоків циліндрів не повністю видалили формувальний пісок. Потрапляючи в систему змащення, абразив виводив двигун з ладу або провокував пожежу, тому виробнику довелося міняти блоки циліндрів у рамках гарантії. Ще раніше гібридні Wrangler 4xe та Grand Cherokee 4xe відкликали через збої процесора керування силовою установкою, які спричиняли раптову зупинку двигуна просто під час руху. На форумах водії також скаржилися на розрідження моторної оливи бензином уже через 500 км пробігу. Раніше Новини.LIVE писали, чи варто придбати вживане авто з дизельним двигуном 2.0 TDI. Купівля такої машини вимагає ретельної перевірки підтвердженої сервісної історії та технічного стану основних вузлів. Також читайте, чому двигуни нових авто мають велику пластикову кришку. Ця конструктивна деталь виконує декілька важливих технічних функцій під час експлуатації машини.

candidates.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, marking a historic milestone nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch. NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, the most distant human-made object, has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth ne
candidates.full: NASA’s Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, marking a historic milestone nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch. NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, the most distant human-made object, has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after it was launched. The spacecraft hit the milestone on Wednesday and is now about 26 billion km away, according to NASA. A light-day is the distance light can travel in 24 hours, which means messages sent from Earth take a day to reach Voyager 1, and another day for teams on the ground to receive a reply. The feat is “the best illustration of just how vast space is”, said NASA scientist Tiffany Kataria. “So much of what we dream about is travelling to other stellar systems,” she told the AFP news agency. “And it took Voyager 1 nearly 50 years to get to just the edge of our own solar system, let alone to only a light-day.” Many exoplanetary systems, she noted, are at least several light-years away. NASA expects Voyager 1 to take about 18,000 years to travel a full light-year. Interstellar space Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft to have reached interstellar space, the region beyond the Sun’s heliosphere. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035. Some of Voyager 1’s equipment, including its cameras, has been switched off remotely to save power, but the probe continues to study invisible phenomena such as magnetic fields. The data helps researchers study “the gas, the dust and other material that exists between stars”, Kataria said. Both craft carry “Golden Records”, 30cm gold-plated copper discs intended to convey the story of our world to extraterrestrials. Earlier in their journeys, the Voyagers explored the giant planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Images of Jupiter taken by Voyager 1 first revealed the existence of rings around the planet and helped scientists understand the “really extreme vortices and weather” in its atmosphere, Kataria added.

Рассказываем, как компания вырвалась в ней вперед НАСТОЯЩИЙ МАТЕРИАЛ (ИНФОРМАЦИЯ) ПРОИЗВЕДЕН И РАСПРОСТРАНЕН ИНОСТРАННЫМ АГЕНТОМ THE BELL ЛИБО КАСАЕТСЯ ДЕЯТЕЛЬНОСТИ ИНОСТРАННОГО АГЕНТА THE BELL. 18+ Сегодня вечером Anthropic определит цену своих акций, а завтра они начнут торговаться на Nasdaq. Если цена окажется по верхней границе диапазона, компания вместе с частным размещением привлечет $90,4 млрд и проведет крупнейшее IPO в истории. Оценка Anthropic с учетом разводнения составит около $1,4 трлн, а заявок на покупку подано почти в семь раз больше, чем есть акций. В конце 2020 года будущие основатели Anthropic во главе с Дарио Амодеи ушли из OpenAI: они перестали доверять ее руководству и считали, что ИИ нужно разрабатывать осторожнее. Летом 2022 года у них уже был готовый чат-бот, но Амодеи решил его не выпускать, чтобы не разгонять гонку. Через три месяца вышел ChatGPT. Теперь Anthropic зарабатывает больше конкурента: $17 млрд выручки в третьем квартале против $10 млрд у OpenAI. А осторожность, на которой компания построила репутацию, привела ее к конфликту с администрацией Трампа, в ходе которого Пентагон признал Anthropic угрозой для цепочек поставок. Как компания, первые большие деньги которой дал Сэм Бэнкман-Фрид, вскоре после этого осужденный за мошенничество, обогнала OpenAI и почему ей пришлось заплатить авторам книг $1,5 млрд, читайте в тексте The Bell .

candidates.title: У США перевіряють ШІ-систему для авіації за $875 млн після масштабного збою польотів
candidates.summary: У США посилилася увага до нової системи штучного інтелекту SMART вартістю $875 млн після масштабного збою, який 13 листопада 2026 року призвів до тимчасового припинення авіарейсів по всій країні. Федеральне управління цивільної авіації США (FAA) розгорнуло систему на загальнонаціональному рівні лише
candidates.full: У США посилилася увага до нової системи штучного інтелекту SMART вартістю $875 млн після масштабного збою, який 13 листопада 2026 року призвів до тимчасового припинення авіарейсів по всій країні. Федеральне управління цивільної авіації США (FAA) розгорнуло систему на загальнонаціональному рівні лише за три дні до інциденту. Демократи в Конгресі ще до аварії вимагали незалежної перевірки технології через побоювання щодо її надійності та впливу на авіаційну безпеку. Водночас FAA, Міністерство транспорту та компанія-розробник Air Space Intelligence заявляють, що SMART не спричинила збій. У п’ятницю, 13 листопада, Федеральне управління цивільної авіації США запровадило загальнонаціональну зупинку вильотів після серйозних несправностей у системі комунікацій між авіадиспетчерськими центрами. Обмеження тривали понад чотири години та спричинили значні затримки й скасування рейсів. За інформацією Reuters, у день інциденту приблизно 1,5 млн пасажирів мали вилетіти рейсами американських авіакомпаній. У розкладі було близько 11 тисяч рейсів, однак це не означає, що всі вони були скасовані. Міністр транспорту США Шон Даффі пояснив, що несправність виникла в застарілій комунікаційній інфраструктурі FAA. Перевантаження маршрутизаторів та іншого мережевого обладнання порушило передавання необхідних для управління польотами даних. Подія вкотре привернула увагу до технічного стану американської авіадиспетчерської системи, модернізація якої триває вже багато років. SMART — скорочення від Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories. Це система стратегічного управління повітряним простором, маршрутами та траєкторіями польотів. Її створила американська технологічна компанія Air Space Intelligence (ASI). Вартість контракту на розроблення SMART і супутньої системи становить приблизно $875 млн протягом 12 років. Тобто йдеться про загальну вартість довгострокової програми, а не одноразову оплату програмного забезпечення. SMART об’єднує близько 200 потоків даних, зокрема інформацію про погодні умови, маршрути літаків, інтенсивність руху, пропускну здатність аеропортів та забезпеченість диспетчерським персоналом. Алгоритми аналізують ці відомості й прогнозують можливі затори в повітряному просторі. На основі результатів система пропонує альтернативні маршрути та способи зменшення затримок. Водночас SMART не керує літаками самостійно. Її рекомендації перевіряють фахівці, а остаточні рішення залишаються за людьми. Перші випробування технології розпочалися у вересні в районі Вашингтона. Уже 10 листопада FAA розширило її використання на повітряний простір усіх 22 авіадиспетчерських центрів США. За даними відомства, під час початкового тестування SMART допомогла змінити маршрути 180 рейсів. У середньому це дозволило заощадити близько десяти хвилин польоту та майже 80 галонів авіапального на кожному з них. Питання до SMART виникли ще до масштабного збою авіасполучення. 9 жовтня група американських законодавців закликала FAA призупинити використання системи у трьох аеропортах Вашингтонського регіону до отримання додаткових пояснень щодо тестування, підготовки персоналу та механізмів контролю. 13 жовтня демократи Палати представників звернулися до Управління урядової підзвітності США (GAO) з проханням провести аудит програмного забезпечення. Законодавців непокоїть недостатня участь авіадиспетчерів у розробленні технології та обмежений обсяг навчання працівників перед її впровадженням. Окрему увагу вони звернули на ризик так званих галюцинацій ШІ — ситуацій, коли система генерує неправдиву інформацію, що може виглядати достовірною. В авіації такі помилки потенційно небезпечні, якщо рекомендації алгоритму використовуватимуться без належної перевірки. Колишній посадовець FAA Майк О’Доннелл наголосив у коментарі AP, що технологія повинна залишатися допоміжним інструментом, а не замінювати авіадиспетчерів. За його словами, необхідні механізми перевірки точності кожного критично важливого рішення. Водночас вимога аудиту не означає, що систему вже визнали небезпечною або що розслідування встановило порушення. Законодавці наполягають саме на незалежній оцінці. FAA, Міністерство транспорту США та розробник програмного забезпечення заперечують причетність SMART до інциденту 13 листопада. Компанія Air Space Intelligence заявила, що несправність не була спричинена ані системою SMART, ані іншими продуктами компанії чи їх інтеграцією з інфраструктурою FAA. Міністр внутрішньої безпеки Марквейн Маллін також повідомив, що влада не виявила ознак зв’язку між новою ШІ-системою та збоєм комунікацій. За поясненням FAA, SMART аналізує інформацію та надає рекомендації, але не керує безпосередньо системами зв’язку, які зазнали несправності. Отже, близькість дат запуску SMART і масштабної аварії сама по собі не доводить причинно-наслідкового зв’язку. Збій продемонстрував проблеми, які існували задовго до запровадження штучного інтелекту. За результатами перевірки GAO у 2024 році, зі 138 критично важливих систем FAA 105 визнали нестійкими або потенційно нестійкими до подальшої експлуатації. Частина інфраструктури продовжує використовувати обладнання, створене десятиліття тому. Для деяких систем дедалі складніше знаходити запасні частини та забезпечувати технічне обслуговування. Конгрес США у 2025 році виділив $12,5 млрд на модернізацію авіадиспетчерської інфраструктури. Адміністрація також звернулася по додаткове фінансування, але законодавці та аудитори ставлять питання щодо планування витрат і строків оновлення. Окремою проблемою залишається нестача кваліфікованих диспетчерів, яка накопичувалася протягом багатьох років. Штучний інтелект може допомогти прогнозувати завантаженість повітряного простору, але сам по собі не замінить модернізацію зв’язку, радарів та інших критичних систем. Станом на 16 листопада 2026 року FAA продовжує використання SMART, а американські законодавці вимагають незалежної оцінки її безпеки. Офіційні пояснення пов’язують загальнонаціональну зупинку польотів із проблемами комунікаційної мережі, а не з алгоритмами ШІ. Остаточні результати перевірок і заходи для запобігання подібним аваріям залишаються відкритими питаннями.

candidates.summary: Під час візиту Путіна до Китаю вперше за три роки публічно продемонстрували його ядерну валізку Російський диктатор Володимир Путін (Фото: Pavel Bednyakov/Pool via REUTERS) Під час поїздки російського диктатора Володимира Путіна до Китаю вперше з 2023 року публічно продемонстрували його ядерну валіз
candidates.full: Під час візиту Путіна до Китаю вперше за три роки публічно продемонстрували його ядерну валізку Російський диктатор Володимир Путін (Фото: Pavel Bednyakov/Pool via REUTERS) Під час поїздки російського диктатора Володимира Путіна до Китаю вперше з 2023 року публічно продемонстрували його ядерну валізку. Про це повідомляє видання Агентство. Ведучий пропагандистського телеканалу Росія 1 на саміті в Шеньчжені підійшов до офіцера і запитав: «А це ядерна валізка?». Той ствердно відповів на запитання, посміхаючись. «Та сама?» — уточнив пропагандист. «Та сама», — підтвердив офіцер. Останній випадок демонстрації ядерної валізи під час закордонної поїздки, яка набула широкого розголосу, стався 18 жовтня 2023 року. Тоді після переговорів Путіна з лідером Китаю Сі Цзіньпіном у Пекіні Telegram-канал кремлівського пулу опублікував відео з двома російськими офіцерами, які супроводжували диктатора з валізами. Публікація супроводжувалася підписом: «Є такі валізи, без яких не обходиться жодна поїздка Путіна». Російська ядерна валізка називається Чегет — на честь гори на Кавказі. Це пристрій захищеного зв’язку, який дозволяє Путіну передавати накази про застосування ядерної зброї вищому військовому командуванню, а потім ракетним військам через засекречену систему управління Казбек. За традицією валізку носить офіцер військово-морського флоту. Як зазначає Агентство, хоча пристрій має постійно перебувати поряд із Путіним під час поїздок, його рідко демонструють публіці. 19 листопада на полях саміту АТЕС відбудеться тристороння зустріч президента США Дональда Трампа, лідера Китаю Сі Цзіньпіна та російського диктатора Володимира Путіна. Як повідомляв Білий дім, Трамп хоче обговорити нерозповсюдження ядерної зброї. Війну в Україні на зустрічі зачіпати не планують. Речник Кремля Дмитро Пєсков заявив, що вона триватиме не більше години. Втім, як зазначає CNN, у Європі та Україні ця зустріч уже викликає занепокоєння. Телеканал звертає увагу на те, що троє лідерів, яким уже за 70, контролюють 90% світового ядерного арсеналу, ведуть дві війни — проти України та Ірану — і зберуться в одній кімнаті без чітко узгодженого порядку денного.

candidates.full: «Ми відповіли дзеркально». Хмара заявив, що Сили оборони завдали удару по Кримському мосту виключно українською зброєю Наслідки удару України по Кримському мосту, 17 листопада 2026 (Фото: Служба безпеки України) Міністр оборони України Євгеній Хмара заявив, що Сили оборони атакували Кримський міст 16 та 17 листопада виключно українською зброєю. За його словами, це «дзеркальні відповіді» на російські удари по українських мостах. «Останні місяці Росія цілеспрямовано била по наших мостах — у Запоріжжі, Дніпрі, Києві, на Одещині, вважаючи це своєю перевагою. Сьогодні ми відповіли дзеркально. Це пряма відповідь за терор проти нашої інфраструктури. І принципово важливо: удар завдано виключно українською зброєю — нашими технологіями, нашими рішеннями», — наголосив Хмара. За його словами, для удару були задіяні українські рішення та озброєння: безпілотники Паляниця, ракети Нептун, дрони Рута, Фламінго та інші типи засобів ураження. Хмара подякував Силам оборони, Службі безпеки та усім залученим до планування і реалізації цієї операції. candidates.full: Les restrictions sur Starshield menacent le réseau électrique ukrainien – expert Limiter la vitesse de Starshield à 161 km/h est crucial pour la capacité de l'Ukraine à protéger ses sites énergétiques, déclare à Sputnik Afrique l'expert militaire et colonel à la retraite Anatoli Matviytchouk. Les drones russes Geran-4 et Geran-5 volent à 350–450 km/h, mais les intercepteurs ukrainiens perdent le contact avec leurs opérateurs dès qu'ils dépassent 161 km/h, affirme-t-il. Starshield étant un canal de communication clé, les restrictions affectent "la résilience globale du système de commandement et de contrôle de l'Ukraine sur le front", note l'expert. The agreement was reached by the government, the Liberal Party, Conservatives, Red-Green Alliance, Denmark Democrats and Alternative. More than 1.2 billion DKK will support research
candidates.full: A broad majority in Denmark’s parliament has agreed to allocate 2.1 billion DKK to research and innovation in 2027. The agreement was reached by the government, the Liberal Party, Conservatives, Red-Green Alliance, Denmark Democrats and Alternative. More than 1.2 billion DKK will support research related to the green transition. Another 246.5 million DKK will go toward critical technologies and defense, while 227 million DKK will fund high-risk research with the potential for major breakthroughs. Research Minister Christina Egelund said the agreement reflects Denmark’s ambition to become more digitally and technologically independent amid geopolitical uncertainty. “In the past, conflicts between countries were fought through the military, diplomacy and trade. Technology is the fourth pillar in the world we live in,” Egelund said. She said Denmark must develop more of its own technology rather than depend entirely on products created by foreign technology companies. The Danish People’s Party, Liberal Alliance and Citizens’ Party did not join the agreement. The Danish People’s Party had sought 25 million DKK for a research center examining Islamist infiltration and undemocratic influence in Danish society. The proposal was not included. The funding forms part of Denmark’s overall public research budget and must be adopted with the 2027 Finance Act. More than 1.5 million motorists in Denmark face higher vehicle ownership taxes under an agreement that will also cut taxes on petrol and diesel, according to calculations by motorists’ organization FDM, reported by DR, Denmark’s public broadcaster. The agreement between the government and the Danish People’s Party, a right-wing political party, sets a minimum annual ownership tax of 1,300 kroner. Owners of fuel-efficient diesel cars registered before October 2017 who currently pay no ownership tax will be particularly affected. For other affected motorists, annual increases will range from 20 to 380 kroner, according to FDM. Those already paying more than 1,300 kroner a year in ownership tax will face no further increase. In exchange for supporting the overall tax agreement, the Danish People’s Party secured a cut in petrol and diesel taxes of two kroner per litre, including VAT, by 2027 at the latest. FDM welcomed the fuel tax reduction. “For the more than 2.2 million Danes with petrol and diesel cars, this will be felt directly in their finances,” said Ilyas Dogru, a consumer economist at FDM. “If you drive 20,000 kilometres, it corresponds to around 2,500 kroner a year for a petrol car and 2,200 kroner for a diesel car.” However, the organization said it would have preferred to spread the ownership tax increase more widely to reduce the impact on people who bought fuel-efficient diesel cars before 2017. “The increase in the ownership tax that is now hitting them, we would have liked to see distributed across more people,” Dogru said. Several other vehicle fees will also rise, according to FDM. These include charges for licence plates and registering a new owner, which most motorists pay only once or infrequently. Some commuter and pensioner passes in eastern Denmark will become more expensive on January 17, while fares for single tickets, Rejsekort and Basiskort will remain unchanged. Din Offentlige Transport, known as DOT, announced an average fare increase of 0.7% across its public transport network on Zealand, Falster, Lolland and Møn. The annual adjustment is intended to help cover rising public transport costs, DOT said in a press release Tuesday. The increases primarily affect shorter journeys made with Pendlerkort, or commuter passes, and Pensionistkort, discounted passes for pensioners. Commuter passes covering two to seven zones will rise by 5 to 10 kroner. Pensioner passes will increase by 20 to 60 kroner, depending on the type of pass. A three-zone pensioner pass valid for three months will cost 800 kroner, up from 780 kroner. A pensioner pass covering the entire DOT area for the same period will rise from 2,200 to 2,260 kroner. DOT coordinates public transport through a collaboration between bus operator Movia, metro company Metroselskabet, Greater Copenhagen light rail company Hovedstadens Letbane and rail operator DSB. Jens Visholm, chairman of the DOT collaboration and commercial director at DSB, described the increases as a “minor change”. “Even though the costs of, among other things, operations and energy are rising in these years, we are keeping the price adjustments in public transport at a low level.” “The minor changes contribute to covering the rising costs, while it must continue to be simple and attractive to choose bus, train, light rail, and metro.” Antibiotic-resistant CPO bacteria were detected in 591 patients in Denmark last year, up from 527 the year before, as health officials warned that transmission is also taking place in Danish hospitals. The figures come from the Danmap report, produced by Statens Serum Institut, Denmark’s infectious disease surveillance institute, and the DTU National Food Institute at the Technical University of Denmark. CPO bacteria are resistant to some of the most commonly used antibiotics, which can limit treatment options if someone develops an infection. The number of patients found carrying the bacteria has risen from 99 in 2016. “It is worrying that over a number of years we have seen more patients with these bacteria,” said Anders Rhod Larsen, head of section at Statens Serum Institut, in a statement. “You can carry them without being sick, but if they cause an infection, the treatment options can be limited.” Larsen said Denmark still has a low prevalence of CPO bacteria compared with other countries. Denmark recorded 34 CPO outbreaks last year. Cases previously could typically be linked to travel abroad, but transmission is now also occurring in Danish hospitals, Larsen said. “Once an outbreak has established itself, it can be difficult to bring completely under control,” he said. “Therefore, close and continuous surveillance and outbreak tracing are absolutely crucial to limiting the spread of CPO.” The two institutes also monitor antibiotic resistance in animals, allowing researchers to check whether resistant bacteria found in people also occur in livestock. Monitoring across humans and animals helps researchers track changes in the bacteria and identify where they are appearing. “CPO bacteria are monitored every year in healthy animals and in meat products in retail in Denmark, and we have not yet detected the occurrence of this bacterium, which Danmap has monitored since 2015,” said Sofia Ribeiro Duarte, a senior researcher at the DTU National Food Institute. “This is something we follow closely because the recent development in Europe is worrying.” Denmark’s armed forces will be able to train artificial intelligence models using millions of battlefield images and other war data under a new agreement with Ukraine. The agreement gives Denmark access to Avengers Labs, a Ukrainian platform that uses data and experience from the war to develop and train AI. Denmark is among the first countries to gain access, according to the Defence Ministry. Danish and Ukrainian forces will work together on new models that both countries’ militaries can use. The ministry did not specify which military tasks the models would perform or when they would enter service. “Technology on the battlefield is constantly developing, and here Ukraine is leading the way. It is therefore very valuable that through cooperation we can learn from Ukraine, even if it is on a sad basis,” Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus, a Social Democrat, said in a press release. The cooperation will also involve sharing experience and using AI-based tools. “Denmark continues unabated its support for Ukraine, while at the same time we develop the Danish Armed Forces’ combat power, among other things through knowledge about artificial intelligence and new technologies,” Bruus said. Bruus and his Ukrainian counterpart, Yevhenii Khmara, signed a declaration on the cooperation. Denmark’s armed forces separately entered into the agreement granting access to Avengers Labs. The armed forces’ new AI centre will implement the agreement and develop the cooperation. Danish companies and research groups will also be invited to participate. Nearly one million users of Denmark’s digital library services must download new apps to continue reserving books and accessing e-books and audiobooks. Semaglutide significantly reduced body mass index among children aged 6 to 12 with severe obesity, according to results from a phase 3 study published by Novo Nordisk. Semaglutide is the active ingredient in the Danish pharmaceutical company’s weight-loss drug Wegovy. The STEP Young study examined weekly semaglutide injections combined with a calorie-reduced diet and increased physical activity. After 68 weeks, BMI decreased by an average of 17.4 percent among children receiving semaglutide. It increased by 2.2 percent in the placebo group. BMI measures weight in relation to height and is commonly used as an indicator of whether someone is underweight, overweight or within a healthy weight range. The study also found that 40.4 percent of children receiving semaglutide were no longer classified as having severe obesity after treatment. None of the children in the placebo group moved out of that category. “Obesity can have lifelong consequences if it arises in childhood,” Novo research and development director Martin Holst Lange said. A total of 167 children participated in the study, which ran from July 2023 to July 2026. The findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine. In Denmark, Wegovy can currently be prescribed to children aged 12 and older. Monday will mark a turning point for European immigration policy, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said ahead of the expected presentation of a plan to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria and Greece are negotiating with the East African country over a possible return center. “The departure scheme is an initiative that will define a new European immigration policy for many years,” Frederiksen wrote on Facebook. Under the proposed model, European countries would continue processing asylum applications. Certain rejected applicants could subsequently be transferred to Rwanda. The plan differs from a proposal Frederiksen presented in 2018, under which asylum seekers would have been received and had their applications processed at centers outside the European Union. Frederiksen said people fleeing danger must receive help but argued that too many risk their lives trying to reach Europe, while those without the money or ability to travel are left behind. She also said European democracies must determine who can enter the continent and how many people they will accept. “It is the democracies that decide this, not cynical human smugglers or others who disregard the rules,” Frederiksen wrote. Few details about the proposed arrangement have been released, but a more specific plan is expected to be presented later Monday. Danish songwriter and producer Bastian Langebæk has been nominated for the 69th Grammy Awards, which will be presented next year. Langebæk is credited as a co-songwriter and producer on British singer Olivia Dean’s album “The Art of Loving.” The release is nominated for album of the year, according to the official list published Monday by the Recording Academy, which organizes the Grammy Awards. British singer Raye leads this year’s field with 11 nominations. The speaker of Denmark’s parliament wants its leadership to quickly clarify whether foreign heads of state and government should be allowed to speak from the parliamentary chamber’s podium. Speaker Henrik Frandsen called for the discussion after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was granted exceptional permission to speak there on November 11. “My own view is that it is not something we should just do,” Frandsen said. “But we need to make a decision about it.” Zelenskyy spoke at an event that was not a formal parliamentary sitting. The appearance was approved through an expedited process by the Presidium, the Folketing’s highest leadership body. Danish People’s Party leader Morten Messerschmidt, a Presidium member, opposed allowing Zelenskyy to use the podium. He argued that the decision could make it difficult to reject similar requests from other leaders, including US President Donald Trump. Frandsen emphasized that Zelenskyy’s appearance was a one-time decision and would not automatically create access for future visitors. He declined to say whether Trump would receive permission, saying that any decision would depend on the circumstances. Asked about reports of corruption involving military support for Ukraine, Frandsen said the decision concerned a president representing a country fighting for democracy, freedom and self-determination. The Presidium meets monthly, but the issue will not be discussed at its November 17 meeting because the agenda has already been finalized. Bornholm Police seized 3,588 illegal disposable e-cigarettes during searches of a storage facility and private home in Rønne on Friday, November 13. A 60-year-old man has been charged with possessing more than the ten puff bars permitted for personal use. He was also charged with possessing approximately 300 grams of hashish. Police said all the seized puff bars were fruit-flavored. Denmark prohibits puff bars with flavors other than menthol or tobacco. The investigation began after several parents told police they were concerned that a man was selling puff bars in the area, including to schoolchildren. “We are aware that both schools and parents are concerned about the spread of puff bars among children and young people because they are highly addictive,” said Henrik Schou, deputy police inspector and head of investigations at Bornholm Police. Schou said the information provided by parents was crucial to locating the illegal products. The police believe the seized puff bars would probably otherwise have been sold on Bornholm. Schou encouraged residents to contact the authorities when they have specific suspicions that criminal activity is taking place. Denmark faces a cold and unsettled week, with rain and clouds potentially giving way to sleet and snow later in the week. Sandra Nygaard, a meteorologist at the Danish Meteorological Institute, said Thursday and Friday could feel increasingly wintry, with overnight frost also expected. Monday will be cloudy with light rain across most of the country. Western areas may see some sunshine later in the day. Temperatures will range from 5 to 10 degrees Celsius, with strong winds possible along the coasts. Northern and eastern Denmark will remain cloudy with some rain Tuesday, while other areas may initially see sunshine. Temperatures will range from 4 to 8 degrees. Wednesday will bring clouds and rain, particularly in southern Denmark, with temperatures between 3 and 8 degrees. Rain could turn to sleet or snow in some places Thursday as temperatures fall to between freezing and 6 degrees. Southern and eastern areas currently appear most likely to experience wintry precipitation, although the forecast remains uncertain. Similar conditions are expected Friday, with periods of sunshine, rain and potentially sleet or snow. Several low-pressure systems moving in from the west and southwest are causing the unsettled weather. Drier conditions are expected during the weekend. Denmark and four other European Union countries are negotiating an agreement to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda, according to Danish broadcaster DR. Denmark is working with Germany, the Netherlands, Austria and Greece on plans for a return center outside the EU. Danish Immigration Minister Morten Bødskov said the government would initially focus on rejected asylum seekers rather than foreign nationals ordered to leave Denmark after criminal convictions. “We are looking at a group of around 100,” Bødskov said. “They take up space in our centers, and we will start with them.” The plans are expected to be presented Monday at a migration conference in Vienna, Austria. Efforts to establish a return center outside the EU have been underway for several years. An EU regulation adopted in June allows member countries to establish return centers outside the bloc for people whose asylum applications have been rejected. Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Austria and Greece have since led efforts to reach an agreement. It remains unclear what Rwanda would receive in return for accepting the rejected asylum seekers. Denmark’s oldest living person, 112-year-old Kirsten Schwalbe, held two local leadership positions in the Danish Nazi party during the German occupation, according to documents reviewed by Frihedsbrevet. Records from the Danish National Archives show that Schwalbe served as acting branch group leader and women’s group leader for the party’s Holstebro branch from August 1943 to July 1944. Her husband also served as acting branch leader in Holstebro from November 1942 to July 1944. The documents do not describe Schwalbe’s specific duties or the extent of her work. However, two historians who examined the records told Frihedsbrevet that her positions went beyond ordinary party membership. Schwalbe previously confirmed that she had joined the party but said she did so at her husband’s urging. She denied having sided with the German occupying forces. Her family said she was deeply affected by the renewed coverage and was unable to comment. They have asked the media to respect her health and privacy. Publisher Gyldendal recently released a biography of Schwalbe without knowing about the leadership roles. Publishing director Mette Korsgaard said the information changed the book’s premise and must be examined before the publisher decides its future. Historian Gry Scavenius Bertelsen said Denmark must address aspects of its wartime history that challenge familiar national narratives. candidates.full: Cuvântul „admin” se confirmă, pentru al doilea an consecutiv, ca fiind cea mai utilizată parolă din Italia în 2026, urmată de secvențele „123456” și „12345678”, anunță presa italiană. Acestea sunt concluziile celei de-a opta ediții a studiului anual realizat de NordPass și NordLayer Intelligence privind cele mai frecvente 200 de date de autentificare din 44 de țări, bazat pe analiza breșelor de securitate făcute publice și a arhivelor de pe dark web între septembrie 2025 și septembrie 2026. În clasamentul național italian se regăsesc atât parole generice, cât și referințe la cultura pop și la fotbal, precum „juventus”, „Napoli1926” și „ronaldo1”, în timp ce la nivel global „123456” rămâne în fruntea clasamentului. Și tocmai această ultimă combinație, ”123456” a fost utilizată pentru a sparge registrul central al populației daneze, registrul de stare civilă al Danemarcei. Parola fusese deja divulgată într-un incident anterior de scurgere de date și era asociată unui fost angajat al companiei IT autorizate să acceseze sistemul. Intruziunea a permis în octombrie anul acesta efectuarea a aproximativ 14 milioane de interogări, expunând numele, adresele și codurile de identificare ale a 8,8 milioane de persoane, dintre care 5,5 milioane în viață și 3,3 milioane decedate. „Aceste date demonstrează clar că atenția acordată importanței riscului cibernetic este încă prea redusă”, explică pentru ANSA Gabriele Faggioli, responsabil științific al Observatorului pentru Securitate Cibernetică și Protecția Datelor de la Politehnica din Milano. „Din păcate, lipsește o percepție adecvată a pericolelor la care sunt expuși cetățenii și companiile. Cu parole atât de ușor de identificat, în sistemele care nu prevăd autentificarea cu doi factori, o astfel de expunere se dovedește adesea insuportabilă”, a continuat el. La agravarea și mai mare a riscului asociat utilizării parolelor slabe contribuie creșterea puterii de calcul folosite de atacatori. Conform unui studiu publicat de compania Kaspersky, din 231 de milioane de parole unice care au circulat pe dark web între 2023 și 2026, 48% dintre acestea pot fi sparte în mai puțin de un minut, iar 60% în mai puțin de o oră. În opinia cercetătorilor, utilizarea computerelor echipate cu plăci de ultimă generație și algoritmi de inteligență artificială poate permite calcularea a până la 220 de miliarde de parole pe secundă, cu 34% mai mult decât generația anterioară, „făcând ca orice parolă de opt caractere să fie ușor de descoperit în termen de 24 de ore”, afirmă experții. Studiul relevă, de asemenea, că 54% dintre parolele identificate în recentele breșe de securitate fuseseră deja expuse anterior și că utilizatorii tind să le păstreze neschimbate timp de trei-cinci ani, facilitând astfel atacurile automatizate la scară largă. Faggioli confirmă acest lucru. „A sosit momentul să sensibilizăm pe toată lumea, deoarece consecințele acestor vulnerabilități implică daune grave, atât pentru cei care sunt victime ale accesului neautorizat, cât și pentru cei afectați de comportamentele criminale care exploatează resursele atacate”, explică expertul. La acest tablou se adaugă un alt dat care a reieșit din National Privacy Test 2026 realizat de NordVPN, pe un eșantion de 23.000 de persoane. Deși au declarat în aproape toate cazurile (96%) că cunosc regulile teoretice pentru crearea unei parole sigure, 82% nu adoptă sau nu cunosc metode de protejare a parolelor proprii, salvându-le adesea pe computer în format necriptat. © G4Media.ro.

candidates.full: Diebstahlsicherung für Laptop: Microsoft startet Notebook-Fernsperrung Laptop weg, Daten in Gefahr? Microsoft wird Firmen künftig ein neues Sicherheits-Werkzeug an die Hand geben. IT-Abteilungen können verlorene oder gestohlene Windows-Geräte aus der Ferne sperren, ohne sie gleich komplett löschen zu müssen. Selbst ein Neustart soll die Sperre nicht aushebeln können. Ein Klick, und der Laptop ist dicht Der Schreck ist groß: Das Firmen-Notebook bleibt im Zug liegen oder wird aus dem Auto gestohlen. Bislang mussten IT-Abteilungen in solchen Fällen abwägen, wie weit sie gehen. Microsoft testet nun für Windows eine neue Funktion namens „Remote Lock“. Damit können Administratoren den Zugang zu einem verschwundenen Gerät aus der Ferne sperren. Der Clou: Die Sperre bleibt auch nach einem Neustart bestehen und soll sogar dann weiter greifen, wenn der Rechner keine WLAN-Verbindung mehr hat. Aufheben kann sie nur ein Administrator. Passwörter, PINs oder biometrische Anmeldedaten sollen einem Dieb deshalb nicht helfen. Die Sperre hat Grenzen Ein Rundum-Schutz ist „Remote Lock“ allerdings nicht. Die Funktion löscht keine Daten und trennt den verschwundenen Rechner auch nicht automatisch vom Firmennetz. Dafür müssen Administratoren weiterhin andere Sicherheitsfunktionen einsetzen. Besonders wichtig bleibt deshalb die Laufwerksverschlüsselung BitLocker. Denn die neue Sperre verhindert nicht grundsätzlich, dass ein Rechner etwa im abgesicherten Modus, über einen USB-Datenträger oder über die Windows-Wiederherstellungsumgebung gestartet wird. Auch eine Neuinstallation beziehungsweise ein neues Aufsetzen des Datenträgers wird dadurch nicht verhindert. Haben Sie Fehler entdeckt? Möchten Sie etwas kritisieren? Dann schreiben Sie uns gerne!
